newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: REVIEW OF FORECASTS - Australian Q1 inflation data.
newsitem.headline: REVIEW OF FORECASTS - Australian Q1 inflation data.

text.p: Australian March quarter inflation data will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.

Forecasts for the consumer price index (CPI), or headline rate of inflation, centre on a 0.1 percent rise in the quarter and an annual rate of 1.2 percent. Quarterly CPI forecasts range from negative 0.1 percent to a rise of 0.3 percent, leading to annual inflation rate forecasts of between 1.0 and 1.3 percent.

For the key underlying rate, forecasts centre on a quarterly rise of 0.4 percent, to be 2.1 percent higher over the year. Quarterly forecasts range from rises of 0.2 to 0.5 percent. leading to annual forecasts of 1.8 to 2.2 percent.
Recent data and March quarter forecasts are below.
Underly Q3 95 Q4 95 Q1 96 Q2 96 Q3 96 Q4 96
The main factor behind the low CPI is the continuing flow through effects of three cuts in official interest rates last year, as well as the competition inspired cut earlier this year.
If the CPI matches forecasts, it will be the lowest quarterly rise since the September quarter 1992, and the lowest annual rate since March 1994.

If the quarterly movement is negative, as some analysts have forecast, it will be the first instance of deflation since June 1992. The last time the Australian economy recorded negative economic growth was also in the June 1992 quarter, when the economy shrank 0.1 percent.
Underlying inflation is seen remaining moderate, as partial price indicators such as import and manufacturing prices are showing little signs of upward pressure.

As well, the Australian dollar, despite some volatility against the U.S. dollar since the last rate cut in December, has held up well in trade weighted terms, helping keep a lid on inflation pressures.

All up, the underlying consists of just over 51 percent of the the components of the CPI, and it removes many of the volatile components from the CPI, such as mortgage costs, taxes and holiday travel, it fluctuates much less than the CPI.
Between December 1992 and December 1996, the annual headline rate ranged between 0.3 and 5.1 percent, while the underlying rate held to a narrower 1.8 to 3.3 percent range.

Inflation is seen remaining under control through 1997, and combined with some signs of recent softness in economic data, has raised the prospect that there may be room for another rate cut to follow the three in the second half of last year.
Tuesday's "living wage" decision, well below what unions had been seeking, was also seen as a positive for both continued low inflation and interest rates.
However, the general feeling amongst analysts is that the data are more likely to dispel any concerns of a near term rate rise, and point to rates being on hold for some time yet.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
